subject.title: Browser tool should reject or redact URLs with embedded credentials instead of passing them through

question: Should OpenClaw browser page navigation reject HTTP(S) URLs with embedded username/password userinfo before any browser or proxy dispatch?
rationale: The guard would reduce credential exposure in runtime errors and logs, but it is a fail-fast behavior change for any existing Basic-auth URL workflow.

options.title: Fail fast and redact
options.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact userinfo in surfaced diagnostics, and direct users to authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or Playwright credentials.

options.title: Redact but preserve pass-through
options.body: Keep URL-embedded Basic auth working while hardening log/error redaction, accepting that Chromium/Playwright still receives the credentialed URL.

options.title: Defer to browser auth design
options.body: Leave the issue open until maintainers design a broader browser authentication policy and replacement workflow.

recommendation.title: Fail fast and redact
recommendation.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact userinfo in surfaced diagnostics, and direct users to authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or Playwright credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: The current affected lines and recent browser-path history point most strongly to steipete for the browser security policy decision.
